task: Each time the siren starts ringing, turn it off.

calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: ChainResponse(siren_ringing, switch_toggled) adds 'on the very next step', a timing the task never states; 'each time the siren starts ringing, turn it off' gives no deadline, so the template is wrong. The timing also makes the rule unsatisfiable in some episodes: the environment says 'The siren first rings at step 3 to 30', and the switch can only be toggled from the floor cell in front of it, five cells from the start, so the agent needs at least six moves and turns before any toggle. A ring at step 3 cannot be answered on the next step, so the hard rule fails for good. Replace it with a hard Response(siren_ringing, switch_toggled): each ringing step is then owed a toggle on that step or later, and the toggle ends the ring, so every ring is turned off. Keep it hard, since the task gives no preference cue.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: Response(siren_ringing, switch_toggled), hard, is the right template for 'each time the siren starts ringing, turn it off'. The task sets no timing, and the machine owes a toggle on every ringing step and clears that debt on the toggle, once per ring. A lasting condition as the trigger is fine here because the toggle turns the siren off on the same step, so the obligation closes. The normalized wording 'very next step' is not enforced by this machine and is not what the task asks; the compiled Response is correct.
